title: Heterogeneous-Goal Model Uncertainty for Self-Adaptive MAPE-K Security Loops
research_question: Can Bayesian model averaging over multiple candidate environment and threat models improve adaptation decisions in self-adaptive security systems when the MAPE-K loop must optimize heterogeneous goals such as protection, latency, and cost?
hypothesis: Extending model-uncertainty-aware adaptation with heterogeneous goal handling will reduce maladaptive or unnecessary security reconfigurations and improve overall decision quality under shifting operating conditions compared with single-model or single-goal baselines.
motivation: The knowledge base surfaces an explicit open problem: current Bayesian model averaging for self-adaptive systems was evaluated on a robotics case study and future work calls for additional domains plus heterogeneous requirements such as threshold and optimization goals. Security-oriented self-adaptive systems are a natural but apparently unexplored target, where wrong model selection can trigger either under-reaction to threats or costly unnecessary adaptations. This proposal also avoids recently rejected agentic-workflow ideas by targeting a distinct, evidence-backed gap in self-adaptation.
